title: A Systematic Review of the Effectiveness of Algebraic Teaching Interventions: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Synthesis
venue: Nordic Journal of Systematic Reviews in Education
extended_summary:
This paper is a protocol for a systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-synthesis of algebra teaching interventions in K-12 education. The authors aim to identify which interventions improve algebra learning, for whom they are effective, and under what conditions. They also seek to understand which moderators—such as grade level, demographic characteristics, intervention type, delivery mode, and teacher training—explain variation in intervention effects.

The paper does not evaluate a single intervention; instead, it outlines a mixed-methods review process that will synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence from U.S.-based studies published since 1980. The planned review includes randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies with baseline equivalence, and empirical qualitative studies, with outcomes focused on mathematics learning, thinking, and knowledge. The authors also propose an algebraic teaching framework grounded in learning progression theory to classify interventions by algebraic big ideas and thinking practices.

The population of interest is U.S. elementary and secondary students in grades K-12, with attention to diverse backgrounds and subgroup differences such as race/ethnicity, gender, socioeconomic status, and grade level. The context is classroom-based algebra, early algebra, and pre-algebra instruction across schools in the United States and its territories. The main contribution of the paper is methodological: it provides a detailed protocol for analyzing how algebra instruction works and which features are associated with stronger student outcomes, rather than reporting empirical results from an implemented intervention.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review/meta-analysis protocol, not an empirical study reporting results. It outlines planned methods, search strategy, and moderators but provides no analyzed evidence or effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effects are reported because the paper is preparatory/protocol-only. As a result, there is no demonstrated impact on student outcomes in this paper itself.
